llm.summary: The skill largely matches its stated purpose (running a P2P AI-validator node) but its runtime instructions ask agents to perform broad system, network, and third‑party operations (build/run, GitHub actions, API keys, public bootstrap peers, and P2P binary/upgrade behavior) while not declaring several required credentials and with some operational behaviors that increase risk.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the included files: this is a Rust P2P blockchain node intended to run AI-backed validators. The repo sources, RPC endpoint, libp2p networking and AI provider integrations align with the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and other docs instruct agents to clone, build, generate local keypairs, run validators that connect to a public bootstrap peer (168.220.90.95), and grant file system, shell and network access. It also encourages autonomous GH CLI operations (fork/PR/merge), Vercel deployment, and monitoring via system tools. These instructions require broad privileges (filesystem, network, ability to run arbitrary built binaries) and ask agents to handle API keys — yet those env/credential needs are not declared consistently. The README's claim of 'P2P binary seeding' and upgrade/announce workflows (operator keys present in Cargo.toml) is an important attack surface: nodes might receive/relay binaries or upgrades — verify how upgrades are authenticated before running them.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no automatic install spec (the package is instruction-only), which reduces hidden remote install risk. Source code is included in the skill bundle for review. Building from source (cargo build) is recommended by the docs — that is expected. Because there is no downloaded binary from an untrusted URL, install risk is moderate but the build/run step will produce and execute a networked binary on the host, so sandboxing is still required.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The runtime docs regularly reference AI provider API keys (Anthropic/OpenAI/Groq/Together) and show examples using $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / gsk_… but the registry metadata lists no required env vars. The skill.json lists 'ai_provider' as required in conceptual requirements but does not declare specific credential environment variables. Additionally, the docs instruct GH CLI usage which implies a GitHub token but no GH credentials are declared. In short: credential and env requirements are under-declared relative to the actions the instructions ask you to take.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and normal model invocation are used. The skill does not request to be force‑included in every agent run and does not claim to modify other skills or system-wide agent settings. It does create/expect local state (keypair, data dir) which is normal for a node.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to be what it says (a P2P AI validator), but it asks you (or your agent) to clone, build, and run networked binaries and to use API keys and GitHub credentials that are not declared in the metadata. Before installing or running:

- Review the included source (especially update/upgrade, RPC, p2p, and any code that downloads or executes remote binaries). Verify how upgrades/binary seeding are authenticated (operator keys are present in Cargo.toml — confirm these are actually enforced at runtime).
- Never run the validator on your main machine with your real private keys or real production API keys. Create an isolated VM/container or sandbox and use throwaway API keys where possible.
- Keep your validator keypair local and offline when possible; follow the SKILL.md warning to never paste your private key to remote services.
- If you or an AI agent will perform GitHub operations (fork/PR/merge), do not give it broad GH tokens unless you explicitly intend that; prefer human approval for push/merge operations.
- Monitor network activity and limit inbound exposure: run in a firewalled environment and review the bootstrap peer addresses. Consider running first in devnet with low-privilege/test keys.

If you want a stronger assessment change confidence to high, provide the compiled binary or confirm how the 'announce upgrade' and 'p2p binary seeding' flows perform signature verification at runtime (point to the exact code paths).
